Picture this: you're settling into a lie-flat business class seat somewhere over the Atlantic, a glass of something cold in hand, knowing that in 48 hours you'll be waking up in Istanbul — and then, a few days later, continuing onward to Bangkok. Two bucket-list cities. One award booking. One points balance. This is what the Aeroplan stopover sweet spot feels like in practice. It's not a trick or a loophole — it's a deliberately designed feature of Air Canada's Aeroplan program that the vast majority of travelers simply don't know exists. And that gap between awareness and reality is exactly where the ChooseFI community finds its edge. Here's the math that should make your jaw drop. A business class itinerary from North America to Istanbul with a continuing flight onward to Bangkok — two long-haul segments, lie-flat seats, Star Alliance lounges at every connection — would cost somewhere between **$6,000 and $15,000 in cash**. That's a realistic retail range depending on season and how far out you book. Most people never consider it a possibility for a family vacation or a milestone trip because the sticker price puts it in a different universe. With Aeroplan, you're booking that same itinerary — the same seats, the same lounges, the same Turkish Airlines or Thai Airways product — for **75,000 Aeroplan points**. At the low end of the cash price range, that's already **8 cents per point**. At the high end, you're extracting **20 cents per point** from a currency that most people earned by putting groceries on a credit card. The pricing inefficiency here is structural. Aeroplan's partner award chart prices long-haul business class at a fixed rate regardless of cash fare fluctuations. When business class prices spike — around holidays, during peak travel seasons, during major events — your points cost stays exactly the same. You're insulated from the market. That's the FI mindset applied to travel: you've already paid for the trip in points, slowly accumulated through everyday spending, and now you're simply redeeming the stored value. The stopover itself is nearly free. Aeroplan charges just 5,000 extra miles to add a stopover city to a one-way award. That means your Istanbul layover becomes a multi-day stay — at zero additional points cost beyond that small add-on — and you haven't booked a second award at all. One booking. Two destinations. That's the entire premise, and once you see it, you can't unsee it.

The mechanism behind this sweet spot is elegantly simple once you understand it, but it requires knowing three things that most travelers don't: how Aeroplan's routing rules work, what a stopover actually is in the context of an award ticket, and why Star Alliance's global network makes this scalable to almost any destination pair you can imagine.

When Aeroplan relaunched its loyalty program in 2020, it did something remarkable: it eliminated fuel surcharges entirely and published a partner award chart with fixed pricing for flights on Star Alliance carriers. This is critical. When you book Turkish Airlines business class through Aeroplan, you pay the Aeroplan fixed chart rate — not what Turkish Airlines would charge in its own currency or miles program, and not the inflated cash price. That fixed chart is the engine of this redemption.

It has been revealed that for long-haul international business class, Aeroplan's chart prices routing through multiple regions based on your origin and destination — not every intermediate stop. This is the aha moment. Aeroplan determines your award price based on where your journey starts and where it ends, and then allows you to add a stopover in between for just 5,000 additional miles. The stopover city is priced as a pass-through for the purpose of calculating your award zone, not as a second trip.

On a one-way Aeroplan award, you're permitted to add a free stopover — meaning you can stay in an intermediate city for any length of time before continuing to your final destination. That 5,000-mile add-on is essentially the cost of a full additional destination. Compare that to booking a second one-way award from Istanbul to Bangkok, which would cost you another 40,000–55,000 Aeroplan points in business class. The math is decisive.

Industry observers note that the routing must be geographically sensible — you can't fly backwards across the globe — but Aeroplan's allowance for multi-segment itineraries through Star Alliance hubs gives you enormous flexibility. Istanbul (IST) is a Turkish Airlines hub. Bangkok (BKK) is served by Thai Airways and several Star Alliance carriers. Both are Star Alliance partners. Both are bookable through Aeroplan at fixed chart rates with no fuel surcharges.

Booking an Aeroplan stopover award in business class is genuinely one of the more complex redemptions in the travel rewards world, but it becomes manageable when you break it into distinct phases. Here's exactly how to do it.

Start by deciding on your two destinations. Aeroplan stopovers work best when your intermediate city is a major Star Alliance hub that lies geographically between your origin and final destination. In a recent development, A stopover is an intentional break in your journey lasting more than 24 hours at a connecting city. Most airlines treat stopovers as separate tickets, charging full price for each segment. Aeroplan is one of the few programs that allows a free stopover on round-trip awards, letting you explore a connecting city for days before continuing to your final destination. This is fundamentally different from a layover, which is a brief connection of a few hours at an airport. The stopover must be in a city served by a Star Alliance carrier on your routing, and the key is that Aeroplan prices the entire itinerary as one award, not two.

How to Navigate the Tariff Circus

📅 13 Jun 2025 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2431 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, quite accidentally, it looks like we timed our last talk about the stock market pretty darned well.
  • And although stock market volatility doesn’t always come with an easily labeled explanation, this time the reason seems pretty clear: it’s the Tariffs.
  • As our financial world has been whipped around like a circus tent in a hurricane for the last several months, almost everyone who has a stake in this country has been wondering what to make of it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, quite accidentally, it looks like we timed our last talk about the stock market pretty darned well. Back in February 2025, the market put the perfect cap on a multi year climb before stepping onto the wild roller coaster we’re currently riding. Since then it has seen some of the steepest drops and recoveries in history, losing a full 20% of its value at the bottom while somehow managing to end up right back near the peak as I’m writing this.

And although stock market volatility doesn’t always come with an easily labeled explanation, this time the reason seems pretty clear: it’s the Tariffs.

As our financial world has been whipped around like a circus tent in a hurricane for the last several months, almost everyone who has a stake in this country has been wondering what to make of it.

As I write this, we still don’t know the outcome of the worldwide tariff and trade battle that our unpredictable government has unleashed upon the world. But we’re already seeing the results: businesses are bracing for massive changes, currencies and interest rates are reacting, and regular investors like you and me are wondering what the future holds for our early retirement funds. Surveying my own group of friends, the reactions span the whole range of emotions from “this is a giant Nothingburger” to “we’re all totally screwed.”.

So what’s the real answer? To get closer to that, we should start with the most basic question of:.

A tariff is just a sales tax charged by our government on goods which are imported into the country. They are paid by whoever is doing the importing – meaning you if you order something like an e-bike directly from a company in China, or by companies like Amazon, Walmart, or Apple which import products from other countries by the shipload.

In a recent development, but in the end, the tariffs aren’t paid by China or Amazon or Apple. They are paid by you, the end consumer, because if their cost of goods increases, a retailer is of course going to raise their prices to continue to make a profit.

Tariffs also affect companies directly: if Home Depot wants to build a latest store or Chevron needs a new oil rig, the tariffs on imported steel, copper, lumber and a million other components will raise the cost of these construction projects. And they raise the cost of housing, because most of the building materials in houses come from multiple countries as well.

Industry observers note that on average, tariffs will result in higher prices for everything just like any other broad-based sales tax. And just like most other taxes, the overall effect is to slow the economy and reduce our spending power. On the positive side, all that tax money flows into the government’s pocket which could help fund the national budget and even reduce the deficit.

Sources indicate that of course, every government needs at least some tax revenue to function, so it makes sense to use some mix of sales, income and corporate taxes to get there. The most important part is that the levels need to be as low as possible while still keeping the country running well, and as fair and predictable as possible, so that people and businesses have an incentive to work hard and the ability to blueprint far into the future.

According to recent reports, and that’s where our current tariff regime gets it completely backwards. Donald Trump is throwing around random, extremely high tariff numbers as threats, then walking them back and changing them on an almost daily basis..

Whoa, that Sounds Mostly Bad – Is There a Good Side of Tariffs?

Sources indicate that sometimes, a country will use tariffs to protect their own domestic industries. For example, if you put a tax on imported Hondas, then General Motors cars will gain a competitive advantage – so GM will make more money. In this example, most consumers end up losing due to increased prices and decreased selection. But at least domestic auto manufacturers and their employees are happy.

This can be strategic (for example we might want to slap a tax on imported fighter jets to make sure Boeing and Lockheed can remain in business, for national defense purposes.) Or it can be corrupt (a politician might receive funding from kingpins in the steel industry, and in return then push through tariffs on imported steel to protect the profits of US steelmakers.).

It has been revealed that and this isn’t just a Trump or Republican thing either – Joe Biden used tariffs during his terms in an attempt to please swing-state voters. One of the worst examples was a tax on imported solar panel components (which Trump has since raised even further, proving that Boneheadedness can be Bipartisan). These are sheets of cheap glass that literally pump the cheapest energy and easiest wealth into your country for 30 years as soon as you plug them in. Cheap energy lowers everyone’s cost of living while also boosting industry. There is no good reason to block such wealth from flowing across your borders.

Can Tariffs Bring Us More Jobs?

According to recent reports, let’s go back to that hypothetical tax on Hondas, and let’s say it’s a substantial one like $5000. At that level, many buyers will start heading over to the GM dealer next door to consider what he’s selling. Sure, the GM cars may not be as good, but for five grand some people are going to settle in order to save some money.

It has been revealed that because of this, GM’s sales go up. So they hire more employees and build more factories. They might even develop some new models and new technologies in response to all that new demand. More people learn advanced skills and in the best case it becomes a virtuous circle.

Industry observers note that but in exchange for this boom in the auto industry, everyone else has to pay more for slightly shittier cars and trucks. Higher vehicle prices means Amazon will have to spend more on their delivery fleet, so they will raise prices slightly on everything they sell. Somewhere a startup company or a medical breakthrough will be just a bit less likely to happen, because they are operating in an environment that is just a bit more expensive and a bit less efficient.

Recent findings suggest that on top of that, with GM liberated from the hassle of competing with Honda, it will have less incentive to innovate and streamline itself. So its overall trajectory will be slower and less efficient even if its profits are higher.

This big picture effect is why most economists agree that tariffs should be used very sparingly. They almost always cause unexpected damage, decrease overall employment and slow down an economy, but sometimes (like for food security or national defense) those costs are worth paying.

So Why is Donald Trump Throwing Around Tariffs Like They Are The Best Thing Ever?

This has been confusing to almost everyone. If you take him at his word, he appears to have a Bizarro Opposite Universe belief system about economics. Donald has claimed in speeches that the tariffs will somehow make us wealthier. He’s focusing on the first-order effects like GM hiring more workers, while completely ignoring the fact that everything else in the country gets less efficient in exchange.

In a recent development, but when he announces larger tariffs, share prices go down, because everyone who actually runs or invests in US companies knows that of course they will make less money on average. When tariffs are paused or reduced, share prices go back up. Yet he keeps wielding the threats and we go back and forth.

It seems to be obvious to everyone except Donald himself that Tariffs are just a national sales tax rather than some clever sneaky strategic weapon, which leads to various theories that okay, maybe he knows that too but is just pretending in order to gain some influence.

The basic theory goes like this:.

So right now our entire economy is subject to the whims of a single person.. And as long as this is the case, we’re just the same as any other dictatorship – something our constitution was supposed to prevent with the whole “three independent branches of government” thing.

Recent findings suggest that but presidents have tried to break out of their constitutional cage and get more power many times in the past, and this is just the latest example. The real test will be if our system eventually manages to stop this abuse and put itself back in balance as it always has in the past. You can already see this fight beginning to play out in our court system, in this Economist article:.

How Big are the Tariffs Right Now?

It has been revealed that even without the 145% nonsense numbers that were thrown around a few months ago, they are still far higher than they have been in the last 75 years or more. While it would be hard to pin down the current numbers in a stationary blog post like this one, the key thing to remember is that our current US economy is built around very low tariffs and relatively free trade.

Why haven’t I noticed Prices Going Up Yet?

While the US economy is fueled by a constant stream of cargo ships, as a whole we function like the biggest cargo ship of all: we have a huge inventory and it takes a while to change directions.

So in normal times, we already have several months of inventory of most things in the country. And then when all this drama started, importers started placing even more orders to stockpile things in advance before the tariffs hit. And now that they are in place, we’re importing a lot less stuff.

Industry observers note that for now, we’re still using up the stockpiled inventory, but imports have dropped significantly so we’re promptly running out of cheap goods. If that happens, we will probably start seeing shortages and price increases throughout this summer or fall. For some things like plastic party trinkets, we can do just fine without. But if we lose access to core useful things like tools and machinery, the economic consequences will be much less fun.

The Dark Side and the Bright Side.

The most important phrase to remember in US politics and economics is the phrase “This too shall pass.” The only mystery right now is that we don’t know exactly how it will pass. So we could sketch out a few scenarios:.

1) The current crazy-high tariffs really do stick around:.

I personally think this is the less likely scenario because nobody really wants it. But just as a thought experiment, it might go something like this:.

2) They do end up being just a negotiating tactic and we go back to mostly low tariffs.

In other words, the best way to win the tariff game is not to play it.

Just as much of US prosperity is built upon our huge population of 330 million people living in 50 states with open borders and no trade restrictions, all (friendly) countries of the world can benefit from the free exchange of goods, services and even people. We’re all human beings and if we treat each other with a collaborative respect, we all grow richer.

Epilogue: Is it Almost Over Already?

I started writing this article on April 2nd, when Donald revealed his “Liberation Day” and the stock market reacted with the biggest drop since 1932. Some people panicked and locked in big losses despite decades of warnings from your favorite financial bloggers, like this unfortunate soul in the comments to a JL Collins post:.

But as I watched over the next two months, we have bounced our way back up – with each drop in proposed tariffs triggering a corresponding increase in stock prices (a measure of investor enthusiasm of how bright our future looks).

Right now, the US stock market is just about back to its all-time high. This doesn’t match with our current level of tariffs, which are still about seven times higher than they were before the circus opened. But it highlights that investors believe it’s all going to end with a truce and a resumption of free-ish international trade.

Recent findings suggest that if they’re wrong, the roller coaster ride will still have some more fun in store for us. But as long as we eventually end our current experiment in “emergency” tariff dictatorship and get back to functioning as a democracy, things should be just fine in the long run. I’m still 100% invested myself, so that’s where I place my bet.

The Biggest Lesson: Don’t Form Your Opinions Based on News Headlines.

Decades ago in a brighter age of journalism, there may have been a time when headlines were designed primarily to inform us, with just a bit of sizzle and spice to pull in our attention. Unfortunately, nowadays the priorities have flipped where the primary goal is attention, and accuracy carries little or no weight. Even a totally inaccurate article makes money for the publisher.

So while Democrats and Republicans like to do battle over which media sources are biased, in reality they’re all wrong: all click-funded commercial media is biased – sometimes politically but even more importantly biased towards generating outrage and fear, because those generate more money.

There are two solutions to this:.

1) Either ignore the media completely and focus on your own life, or.

2) Become a subject matter expert on things you really care about, and then read the original sources whenever you want to learn about something.

Recent findings suggest that I mostly practice option #1, but as a science and technology nerd I get into #2 in just the areas I find most interesting. And it’s amazing how the more deeply you understand a subject, the more you see just how wrong most media stories are about your area of expertise. Which means they’re probably pretty wrong about almost everything.

So as always, with this lesson learned it’s time to shut down that phone and laptop, exhale all our worries and get back outside with your real-life family and friends. See you in a few months!

Military Retirement Pay – The TSP Now Matters as Much as the Pension

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Under the military’s Blended Retirement System, 20 years earns a pension of 40% of your highest 36 months’ average basic pay, against 50% under the old High-3 blueprint.
  • If those 36 months average $60,000 of basic pay, a 20-year career pays $24,000 a year under the blended system and $30,000 under High-3.
  • Military OneSource says about 81% of members under High-3 leave with no retirement benefit, and it expects about 85% under the blended system to leave with one.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Under the military’s Blended Retirement System, 20 years earns a pension of 40% of your highest 36 months’ average basic pay, against 50% under the old High-3 blueprint. Put at least 5% of your basic pay in the Thrift Savings Plan to get the government’s full 5%, yours after two years even if you leave before 20.

If those 36 months average $60,000 of basic pay, a 20-year career pays $24,000 a year under the blended system and $30,000 under High-3. High-3 still covers most members who joined before 2018 and didn’t opt in.

Most members never get that far. Military OneSource says about 81% of members under High-3 leave with no retirement benefit, and it expects about 85% under the blended system to leave with one. The difference is the Thrift Savings Blueprint, the military’s 401(k), where the government puts in 1% of basic pay and matches up to 4% more.

Recent findings suggest that between 7 and 12 years of service, continuation pay gives active-duty members at least 2.5 times their monthly basic pay for agreeing to serve at least 3 more years. At retirement, you can take 25% or 50% of your pension up to age 67 as a discounted lump sum, and your monthly check shrinks by that share until 67. The Survivor Benefit Strategy costs 6.5% of the pension you cover and pays your spouse 55% of it after you die.

Industry observers note that after you retire, a yearly cost-of-living raise keeps the pension in step with consumer prices. It’s taxed as federal income, though many states exempt it, as the Military Officers Association of America’s state tax map reveals. You and your family can stay on TRICARE health coverage for a yearly enrollment fee by enrolling within 90 days of retiring, then switch to TRICARE For Life alongside Medicare at 65.

A medical retirement pays a pension before 20 years to members found unfit for duty with a Defense Department disability rating of at least 30%. VA disability pay is tax-free, but by law it reduces the pension dollar for dollar. Retirees with 20 years and a VA rating of 50% or more get the full pension back, and a combat-related disability can qualify for a separate payment that covers some or all of the cut.

Use the Defense Department’s Blended Retirement System calculator to project your own pension before you sign for continuation pay or pick a lump sum.

Keep Savings in the Bank During a Recession – Cash at Home Is Barely Insured

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (463 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, leave your savings in the bank when a recession looms, and keep your balance at each bank under the $250,000 insurance limit.
  • Industry observers note that bank failures do rise in a recession, which is why pulling your savings out can feel like the careful move.
  • The FDIC, the federal agency that insures bank deposits, says no depositor has lost insured money since it was founded in 1933.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, leave your savings in the bank when a recession looms, and keep your balance at each bank under the $250,000 insurance limit. Insured deposits have been paid in full through every downturn, while cash at home can be stolen or burned and gets only $200 of coverage under a typical homeowners policy.

Industry observers note that bank failures do rise in a recession, which is why pulling your savings out can feel like the careful move. It actually takes money out of a federally insured account and leaves it where almost nothing protects it.

The FDIC, the federal agency that insures bank deposits, says no depositor has lost insured money since it was founded in 1933. That record held through the last massive wave, when 465 banks failed from 2008 through 2012, by the FDIC’s count. Federally insured credit unions have similar coverage through the National Credit Union Administration, and none of their members has lost a cent of insured savings either.

Sources indicate that cash at home has no such backing. A burglar or a house fire can take all of it, and it earns nothing while inflation shrinks what it buys. The FDIC’s disaster guide suggests depositing large sums at an insured bank and holding a small amount of cash for food and supplies, since ATMs and credit cards may not work in a disaster.

Say a family withdraws $20,000 in a panic and hides it in a closet. If a fire or a break-in takes it, a typical homeowners policy covers only $200 of cash, according to the nonprofit Consumers’ Checkbook, so at least $19,800 is gone. Kept in an insured savings account paying 3.5% a year, the same $20,000 would be covered in full and earn $700 in its first year.

According to recent reports, hold your emergency fund, sized to your bare-bones bills, in an insured high-yield savings account. FDIC coverage is $250,000 per depositor, per bank, for each ownership category, meaning how you own the account, such as alone or jointly.

Total your balances at each bank before you move a dollar, and send only the amount over the limit to an account at a second insured bank.

Compare the best high-yield savings accounts for an insured place to keep your savings.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that managing your money isn’t just about earning more. It’s also about stopping unnecessary losses. In today’s digital economy, recurring subscription charges (streaming services, premium apps, trials, memberships) quietly drain money each month. Most people spend hundreds, or even thousands, annually on services they don’t use. Subscription manager apps help you see recurring charges, track billing cycles, and cancel those you no longer want.

Before choosing an app, know what features matter most:.

Rocket Money is one of the most well-known subscription managers. It scans your linked bank and credit accounts for recurring charges and displays them on a clear dashboard. People like it for its ability to detect subscriptions and assist with cancellations directly in the app, a major time-saver for busy people.

Why it stands out• Automatically detects recurring payments• Lets you cancel unwanted subscriptions directly from the app• Includes extra budgeting tools and spending alerts• Trusted security with read-only bank access.

Who it’s for: People who want the fastest way to spot and stop unwanted recurring charges without manually entering every service.

Trim is another financial assistant that scans transactions and flags recurring charges. While subscription tracking is a smaller part of its feature set, it also provides bill negotiation support and money-saving alerts. Many users like Trim because it reaches out on your behalf about subscriptions via text or in-app messaging.

Why it stands out• Recurring transaction detection• Alerts about unusual subscriptions or trials converting to paid• Bill negotiation tools beyond basic subscription tracking.

Who it’s for: Customers who want automation plus help reducing bills and optimizing spending.

In a recent development, pocketGuard is primarily a budgeting app that includes subscription tracking as part of a broader financial overview. Instead of being solely a subscription manager, it integrates recurring expenses into your overall budget, helping you get a full picture of your finances.

Why it stands out• Syncs automatically with financial accounts• Highlights recurring expenses in the context of your whole budget• Helps track cash flow and affordability.

Who it’s for: People who want subscriptions tracked inside a complete personal finance dashboard.

Monarch Money offers robust financial planning tools: budgets, goals, net worth tracking, and more, with subscription visibility included in the package. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • A pack a day costs your local pack price times 365, and vaping costs a week’s pods or e-liquid times 52.
  • Take a pack-a-day smoker whose plan covers the patches they quit with.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Quit smoking or vaping and you stop spending on packs or pods, often thousands of dollars a year, and later pay less for life and health insurance. Most health plans must cover quit-smoking counseling and medication at no cost, so ask your doctor to prescribe nicotine patches, and call 1-800-QUIT-NOW for free coaching.

Work out your own yearly cost. A pack a day costs your local pack price times 365, and vaping costs a week’s pods or e-liquid times 52.

Take a pack-a-day smoker whose plan covers the patches they quit with. At $9 a pack, they keep about $3,300 in the first year, before any insurance savings. Most life insurers charge nicotine owners, vapers included, higher premiums than nonsmokers pay for equal coverage. Insurers selling plans on HealthCare.gov and state marketplaces can add up to 50% to a tobacco user’s premium.

Smoke also counts against a car or a house when you sell it. Its odor can be hard and expensive to clean out of a car. A 2008 San Diego State University study found nonsmokers asked 7% to 9% more for their used cars than smokers did for comparable ones. In a Drexel University survey, 96% of Philadelphia-area realtors said a house where people smoke is harder to sell.

In a recent development, under federal guidance, a job-based or marketplace plan complies by covering at least two quit attempts a year at no cost. Each attempt includes four counseling sessions and 90 days of FDA-approved medication, from nicotine patches and gum to prescription pills.

That coverage includes over-the-counter patches and gum only with a prescription, so ask your doctor for one instead of buying them off the shelf. Then call 1-800-QUIT-NOW, which connects you to your state’s free quitline. Its coaches help vapers too, and some state quitlines give callers free medication.

The insurance savings take longer. For marketplace plans, tobacco use means regular use in the past six months, so once you’ve gone six months without tobacco, you can answer no to the tobacco question on your next application and drop the surcharge. Most life insurers want 12 months without nicotine before they’ll rate you a nonsmoker, and patches and gum count as nicotine.

So write down the day you stop all nicotine, and a year later, ask your life insurer to reprice your policy at nonsmoker rates.

Are you trying to win the Mega Millions, but your numbers never seem to come up? It may be time to look for better ways to make money. Fortunately, you can earn extra cash without going and getting a “real job.”.

What are the best ways to avoid sitting in a cubicle all day? Some money-making strategies require an upfront investment, while others let you earn money in your free time with the help of apps.

Read on to learn the best ways to earn cash without a regular 9-5 job, plus tips on how almost anyone can get started.

In a recent development, one of the easiest ways to earn money is by signing up to participate in market research studies. You won’t make much, a few dollars here and there, but you can create a free account and get started within minutes.

You’ll be paid in PayPal cash or gift cards for sharing your opinion and completing other tasks online.

E-Poll Market Research is one of the top companies to consider for this type of work. They make it easy to create an account and answer survey questions.

However, there are plenty of other options to consider, including:.

While market research gigs won’t make you rich, it’s something you can do during your spare time.

If you have a book idea, turning your story into an eBook can help you earn passive income without a regular job. Kindle Direct Publishing can even help you format your book for Kindle, at which point you can market and sell your book to millions of potential readers who shop on Amazon.com.

Recent findings suggest that how much can you earn writing eBooks? That depends on how many books you write, how much you sell them for, and how successful you are at marketing your book. Selling 20 books per month with a profit of $7 per book would net you $140 per month and $1,680 per year.

Meanwhile, selling 100 books per month at $7 per book would net you $700 per month and $8,400 per year. Need a little inspiration? Here’s an article that demonstrates you how to make your first $1,000 selling eBooks.

Recent findings suggest that you can earn a lot of money by starting a blog or niche website and monetizing it. I should know. I started Good Financial Cents more than a decade ago, and have earned millions of dollars through the monetization of this site since its earliest days.

Recent findings suggest that how do you make money blogging? Earning real income with a website isn’t as easy as it looks, but there are plenty of monetization strategies you can try.

Here are the most common ways blogs make money:.

In a recent development, if you’re curious about what it takes to earn money blogging, consider signing up for my Make 1K Challenge. It’s free and can help you earn your first $1,000 online with some of the blog monetization strategies I’ve already mentioned.

You could argue that freelance work is like a regular job, but working at home and on your terms is much different from traditional employment. The fact is, most freelancers are fully remote – they can work from anywhere in the world with a laptop and an internet connection.

Sources indicate that plus, they can hire and fire clients based on their personal needs and preferences, and their income potential is unlimited. According to ZipRecruiter, freelancers in the U.S. average $63.53 per hour.

In a recent development, of course, you’ll need a marketable skill to find paid work as a freelancer. This could be freelance writing, design skills, marketing expertise, or something else.

You can use several websites to market your skills as a freelancer, including:.

HealthyWage makes it possible to earn money while you lose weight. You won’t earn a ton of cash through the app, but you can earn a few dollars and use it to supplement other income you have.

Recent findings suggest that the more weight you lose, the more money you can make. For example, the HealthyWage website claims some of their clients who lost more than 100 pounds managed to earn anywhere from $1,400 to $3,000.

However, the HW weight loss calculator indicates potential earnings of $578 to $828 for people who only have 15 pounds to lose.

According to recent reports, if you have a car you rarely use and want to earn some side income, you can consider renting it out with Turo, a ride-sharing platform that connects car owners with people who need a short-term rental. You can set your price, although you’ll have more success if you price your car competitively.

Nicer vehicles in high-demand areas can easily fetch rates that surpass $100 per day through this platform. Turo notes that in-demand cars rented out regularly can bring in anywhere from $10,000 to $20,000 per year in net profit.

In a recent development, plus, almost anyone can rent out their car provided it meets the guidelines of the Turo platform. Your car must be 12 years old or newer with less than 130,000 miles. It must be worth less than $200,000 (no Lambo’s), and you must also meet Turo’s auto insurance requirements.

Do you have a spare bedroom in your home that you never use? Maybe you have a basement or garage apartment you could fix up and begin renting for a profit?

Either way, Airbnb lets you rent out rooms and other spaces in your home on any dates you prefer. You must let renters know they’re renting a room in a home vs. an entire apartment or house and provide as much additional detail as possible.

The amount you can earn will depend on where you live and the type of accommodation you can offer. However, expensive cities like Chicago, New York, and San Francisco have plenty of rooms for rent that go for well over $100 per night.

You may not have an entire room you can rent, but even if you have some storage space, Neighbor.com allows you to rent it out to others in need.

Common spaces rented through this platform include.

The Neighbor.com platform makes it easy to advertise your unused space so that people nearby can inquire if they’re interested. Also, note that the platform offers insurance that can protect you if some of your client’s items are damaged or stolen while in your care.

Industry observers note that how much can you make renting out extra space? It depends on how much space you have to rent and where it’s located. However, Neighbor.com shows a range of rental space options that cost anywhere from $20 to $100+ per month.

Industry observers note that investing in dividend stocks is one of the best ways to earn money without a regular job. Many early retirees find a way to live and pay bills based solely on the dividends they receive from various stocks.

But what exactly is a dividend stock? For the most part, they are regular stocks but with a track record of sharing their profits with investors through dividends.

Dividends can also be earned in exchange-traded funds (ETFs) or mutual funds, and they can be significant once you build up a large portfolio.

Since dividends are paid by profitable companies, they tend to be seen as less risky for investors. If you’re curious about what it takes to get started with this strategy, this post explains how to invest in dividend stocks.

It has been revealed that housesitting is an option if you’re somewhat mobile and can move from place to place. Generally, you can find house-sitting gigs through word of mouth, referrals, or online portals like Craigslist.org or Facebook Marketplace.

In a recent development, that said, not all house-sitting gigs are paid. Some offer the potential for exotic travel instead and free lodging for a week to several months.

Industry observers note that either way, a website called TrustedHousesitters is the best place to find house-sitting gigs. Some jobs posted are for house-sitting only, while others require house sitters to provide basic care for pets or plants.

Industry observers note that if you have serious wanderlust and want to travel far and wide, this platform can help make it happen. Many gigs posted online are in countries like Australia, Ireland, France, and Switzerland.

If you love animals and want to earn money taking care of them, several platforms can help turn your dream into a reality.

It has been revealed that for example, Rover.com lets you provide basic care for dogs or cats in your home, or you can pick up dog walking gigs. Another mobile app, called Wag!, lets you do more of the same.

Industry observers note that you can set your rates for all types of work through these platforms, and your availability. While earnings vary by location and job, most people watch dogs and cats for anywhere from $40 to $100 per night.

According to recent reports, real estate investing may seem like a pipe dream if you hope to earn income without a job but hear me out. There are many ways to earn income through real estate without owning physical property or dealing with the hassles of being a landlord.

It has been revealed that you can invest in real estate investment trusts (REITs) that let you build wealth over time. You can also use a platform called Fundrise to invest in real estate with a minimum investment of $10.

Fundrise lets you purchase eREITs, large investment funds that acquire, own, or operate multi-residential and commercial properties. The income you earn is entirely passive since it handles the work of finding income-producing properties and managing them.

While returns are never guaranteed, Fundrise investors have achieved very solid returns. Investors who use the platform earned an average return of 7.31% in 2020, followed by 22.99% in 2021, 1.50% in 2022 and -7.45% in 2023 (their first down year).

You can earn income on your spare change by investing it using Acorns. The roundup savings app syncs to your debit or credit card rounds up every purchase you make to the nearest dollar, and invests the difference. Once it’s set up, there’s no work on your part.

Industry observers note that most of the money is invested in ETFs and managed by the world’s top investment firms like Vanguard and BlackRock. While this app makes it easy to invest small amounts of money, it’s not free to use. Personal prepares start at $3 per month, while a family plan costs just $5.

If you’re looking for some paid gigs that are relatively easy, consider setting up a profile on TaskRabbit, an online platform that lets you get paid for completing various tasks, such as:.

It has been revealed that projects typically pay between $30 and $100, although some pay significantly more than that. TaskRabbit also lets you pick and choose the jobs you want to take on based on your availability so that you can work entirely on your schedule.

If you love taking photographs and have a knack for getting professional-looking images, you can use your skills and expertise to sell photos online.

Websites like Depositphotos and iStockPhoto pay photographers to supply them with stock photos they can sell to writers, publications, and various online platforms.

It has been revealed that the best part about this side hustle is that you can get started with the equipment you already have. While you can use a professional camera if you want to, many smartphones take professional-quality photos.

According to recent reports, earning a bank bonus is another way to earn money without a regular job, but you’ll need an upfront investment to get started. Most bonus offers require you to deposit a specific amount of money and keep it in your account for up to 12 months.

You may also be required to set up direct deposit to earn a bank bonus, and other terms and conditions may apply.

Where can you find the best bank bonuses? While bonus offers constantly change, you can start by checking with banks like Chase, HSBC, Radius Bank, and Wells Fargo.

Flipping furniture requires some upfront legwork and potentially even some artistic talent, but you can earn a solid income with this strategy if you know what you’re doing.

Essentially, this side hustle requires you to shop at thrift stores, garage sales, and online platforms to find furniture that will ultimately sell for more than you paid.

From there, you can sell the furniture as-is or clean it up and paint it with the goal of fetching an even higher price.

You can make money driving for Uber or Lyft on your own time, picking and choosing the days and hours you want to work.

Not only is rideshare work one of the most flexible side hustles, but you can earn $20 per hour and more with tips.

If you are low on free time but still want to make money without a job, consider selling stuff you don’t need. An array of online platforms makes it a breeze, although some platforms work better for selling.

For example, you can use Poshmark to earn money selling used clothing and accessories, while used electronics tend to sell best on platforms like eBay.com, Decluttr, BuyBackWorld, and Gazelle.

If you have home decor, furniture, or workout equipment to sell, you’ll almost always do better unloading those items locally on Facebook Marketplace.

Sources indicate that starting a YouTube channel is another way to earn money without a job, but that doesn’t mean it’s not work. The fact is, that creating quality videos and building an audience takes a lot of creativity and time. Plus, not everyone who tries to build a YouTube channel will succeed.

It has been revealed that that remarked, you can earn income without a regular job. I know because I have done it with my YouTube channel, Wealth Hacker.

Sources indicate that how much you can earn on YouTube varies quite a bit, but it’s possible to earn thousands of dollars per month. If you’re curious about monetizing videos, my in-depth guide will show you how to make money on YouTube.

Industry observers note that donating plasma is a unique way to earn money without a job, although it’s not very glamorous. DonatingPlasma.org makes it easy to find plasma donation centers in your area, and you can earn as much as $100 for your first donation.

That remarked, subsequent plasma donations typically earn closer to $50. You’ll also be limited by the number of times you can donate plasma within a month. However, it’s possible to use this side gig to earn an extra $500 per month, which you can use to supplement your primary income.

If you are willing to complete various tasks that help regular workers do their jobs, consider becoming a crowd worker. This gig will have you finishing up to-do lists of jobs that don’t require specific technical skills.

For example, you may get paid to proofread documents, label images, patch a resume, complete a form, or complete a data entry assignment.

Several platforms help you find crowd-working gigs, but the best ones include Microworkers and Clickworker.

Recent findings suggest that if you want to do something simple that will get you moving, consider delivering groceries using apps like Instacart or Shipt. You get paid hourly, plus tips and all you have to do is head to the store, purchase groceries according to a list, and deliver them to people in your neighborhood.

The gig is extremely flexible, similar to driving for Uber or Lyft.

Another non-job gig lets you get paid to deliver packages for Amazon.com. You can do this through a platform called Amazon Flex, which promises its drivers anywhere from $18 to $25 per hour.

Recent findings suggest that unlike a regular Amazon job, Flex lets you pick the day and the hours you want to work. To get started, you need to create a free account, get approved, and start reserving blocks of time you want to deliver packages.

In a recent development, finally, you can earn money by selling unwanted or unused gift cards in your possession. This hustle is made easy thanks to platforms like GiftDeals.com and CardCash.com.

It has been revealed that you won’t get the total value of your gift cards, but you should get 90% or more of the gift card balance for each card you sell. While selling gift cards for less than their total value may not seem ideal, it’s better than not using them and getting nothing in return.

Sources indicate that finally, you can earn small amounts of money by signing up with the best online survey sites. Not only is this side hustle as easy as it gets, but you can participate and get paid during your spare time and even on your phone.

Other online survey sites to check out include the following:.

According to recent reports, there you have it, 26 ways to make money without a job. While many of the jobs on our list won’t replace your 9-5, they can be a great way to increase your income so you can pay off debt or break the cycle of living paycheck to paycheck.

The Investments That Hold Up in a Recession – Own Them Before It Hits

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Treasury bonds, cash, and the steadiest stocks have held up best in past recessions, but they protected only the investors who already owned them.
  • Sources indicate that that switch gets the timing backward.
  • That year the S&P 500 lost 37% while 10-year Treasury bonds gained 20%, according to yearly returns compiled by NYU Stern professor Aswath Damodaran.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Treasury bonds, cash, and the steadiest stocks have held up best in past recessions, but they protected only the investors who already owned them. Choose your stock and bond mix and set aside emergency cash while the economy is growing, then rebalance through the slump instead of selling stocks for safety once the news turns bad.

Sources indicate that that switch gets the timing backward. By the time a recession is in the news, you’d be selling stocks after they’ve fallen and buying safe havens after other investors have already pushed their prices up.

The 2008 crash shows the cost. That year the S&P 500 lost 37% while 10-year Treasury bonds gained 20%, according to yearly returns compiled by NYU Stern professor Aswath Damodaran. The National Bureau of Economic Research, which determines when U.S. recessions start and end, didn’t announce that one until Dec. 1, 2008, about a year after it began. An investor who moved from stocks to Treasury bonds at the end of that year then lost 11% on the bonds in 2009, while the S&P 500 gained 26%.

Which haven protects you depends on what drives the downturn. In a crash that sends investors looking for safety and pulls interest rates down, as in 2008 and 2020, high-quality bonds gain while stocks fall. In a drop driven by inflation, as in 2022, rising rates cut the value of bonds already issued, so bonds fall along with stocks. Consumer prices rose 6.5% that year, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reports.

Here’s how each haven did in 2008 and 2020, and where it let investors down:.

According to recent reports, the bonds have to be high quality. Corporate bonds with a middling credit rating, Baa, lost 3% in 2008, the year 10-year Treasury bonds gained 20%.

You can’t tell in advance which kind of downturn is coming, so a mix built for a recession holds both high-quality bonds and cash.

Some ideas pitched as recession-proof rarely belong in an ordinary investor’s mix.

Recent findings suggest that pick a split between stocks and high-quality bonds that you’d stick with if stocks fell 37%, as they did in 2008. Then write your investing rules down, including that split and the date you’ll check it. Keep an emergency fund that covers your bare-bones bills in cash outside the mix, so a layoff doesn’t force you to sell stocks at a low. Money you’ll need within a few years belongs in safe places that earn interest instead.

Recent findings suggest that rebalancing your portfolio through the slump means selling some of what held up to buy more of what fell. Take $100,000 split 60% in stocks tracking the S&P 500 and 40% in 10-year Treasury bonds at the start of 2008, with Damodaran’s yearly returns and no fees or taxes. Three moves at the end of 2008 led to different results by the end of 2009:.

According to recent reports, decide now how far your mix can drift before you rebalance, such as 5 percentage points from your target share in stocks. Then in the next slump, selling what held up to buy what fell is a rule you already wrote, not a call you make in a panic.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that managing money as a household is harder than it looks. Most people use a regular checking account at a big bank, then juggle a separate budgeting app, maybe a savings account somewhere else, and possibly a kids’ debit card on top of that. It’s a lot to keep track of.

Crew is a fintech app that tries to put all of that in one place. It combines a high-yield checking account, built-in budgeting tools, and family banking features – all inside a single app. The goal is to help you organize your money, automate your budget, and earn more interest without switching between apps.

In this Crew review, we cover what it is, how it works, who it’s best for, the key features, pricing, and what real users are saying. If you’re looking for a smarter checking account that does more, this review gives you the full picture.

It has been revealed that crew is a fintech app that tries to put all of that in one place. It combines a high-yield checking account, built-in budgeting tools, and family banking features.

• High-yield checking • Debit cards available for kids• Unlimited budgeting pockets• Cash deposits and mobile check deposit• No monthly fees or minimum balances.

• App-only banking with no desktop login• No physical check writing.

In a recent development, crew is a financial technology (fintech) tech giant based in Lehi, Utah. It was founded by Gentry Davies and Steve Domino, who previously worked at Divvy, a business expense platform acquired by Bill.com. The app launched publicly and has been growing steadily since 2023.

Industry observers note that crew is not a bank. Banking services are provided by Bangor Savings Bank, which is FDIC-insured. Your deposits are held at Bangor Savings Bank, so they are protected up to federal insurance limits – $250,000 for individual accounts and $500,000 for joint accounts.

The app is available on both iOS and Android. A web app is currently in beta.

Crew works well for a wide range of people, but it’s especially useful if you fall into one of these groups:.

Crew may not be the right fit for:.

Crew offers a checking account that earns 2.95% APY on your full balance. This rate applies to every dollar you hold in the account – there’s no minimum deposit requirement and no tiered rate structure.

Why it matters: Most significant bank checking accounts pay close to 0.01% APY. Earning nearly 3% on your everyday checking balance can add meaningful interest over time, especially for families keeping a few thousand dollars in their account at any given time.

Industry observers note that pockets are virtual “buckets” inside your single Crew checking account. You can create as many as you need – for example, one for bills, one for savings, one for a vacation fund, one for groceries.

According to recent reports, why it matters: You don’t need a separate savings account or multiple bank accounts. Pockets let you visually and mentally divide your money without moving it to another institution. You can also lock a pocket in “piggy bank mode” to avoid dipping into it.

According to recent reports, crew’s Autopilot feature lets you create rules that move money automatically based on triggers. Triggers can be events like a paycheck arriving or a balance dropping below a set level, or they can be time-based, like every Friday or the 1st of the month.

Why it matters: Automation removes the discipline requirement from budgeting. You set your rules once, and Crew handles the rest. For example, you can tell Crew to automatically send 10% of every paycheck to your giving pocket, $500 to bills, and keep the rest in checking — without touching the app every payday.

In a recent development, why it matters: Most banking apps bolt on a kid’s account as an afterthought. Crew builds family banking into the core experience. Parents get real-time spending notifications, spend controls, and the ability to set automated allowances.

Parents can set up automatic recurring transfers to a child’s account. You define the amount and the schedule, and Crew handles the delivery.

According to recent reports, why it matters: Automated allowances teach kids about money while removing the “I forgot to pay your allowance” problem for parents. Kids learn what consistent saving looks like in practice.

Every account member gets a Mastercard debit card. You can switch which pocket your card draws from at any time inside the app – or upgrade a transaction after the fact if you accidentally spent from the wrong pocket.

It has been revealed that why it matters: This setup means budgeting is “baked in” to your spending. Instead of tracking what you spent after the fact, you decide which budget category you’re spending from before or at the time of purchase.

You can use your Crew Mastercard at any ATM in the Mastercard, Maestro, or Cirrus networks. Crew does not have its own fee-free ATM network, but it reimburses ATM fees for up to 20 withdrawals per year.

Why it matters: The annual ATM fee reimbursement covers most casual cash people without adding much complexity.

It has been revealed that crew supports outgoing wire transfers. The fee depends on your total account balance.

Incoming wires and standard ACH transfers are processed as usual through the app.

Deposits held through Crew are insured through Bangor Savings Bank, a Member FDIC institution.

This is standard FDIC pass-through insurance. Crew’s website states that pass-through insurance is subject to certain conditions set forth in the deposit agreement.

Recent findings suggest that crew includes an AI-powered financial assistant called Penny. Penny can answer questions about your account, help you set up automations, and give you guidance on your financial situation.

Why it matters: Penny gives users a simple way to interact with their finances through natural language, without digging through menus.

Recent findings suggest that one of Crew’s stronger selling points is its simple, low-fee structure. Here’s a clear breakdown:.

Recent findings suggest that note: APY is variable and may change at any time. The 2.95% rate is the most recent published rate. Always check trycrew.com for the current rate before opening an account.

Opening a Crew account is quick. Most people complete it in under two minutes. Here are the steps:.

To add a family member, go to the Family section of the app and follow the prompts to add a joint owner or create a child account.

The APY is variable, meaning it can change over time. It is not a limited-time promotional rate in the traditional sense; it applies to your full balance, with no minimum or expiration. However, Crew can adjust the rate when market conditions change. The rate has fluctuated over the app’s history (it was as high as 3.7% in early 2025). Referral sign-ups may qualify for a 0.5% APY boost for the first three months.

It has been revealed that cash deposit support has been in development. Some reviews noted it was not yet available at the time of writing, though the feature has been in the works. It’s worth checking the current app version or Crew’s website for the latest on cash deposits before signing up if this is important to you.

In a recent development, you need your legal name, date of birth, physical address, and a tax ID (typically your Social Security number). Most applicants complete the process in under two minutes.

Sources indicate that crew earns revenue in two ways: from the interest it earns on deposits held at Bangor Savings Bank, and from merchant fees when you use your Crew debit card to make purchases. This model is common among fintech companies and allows them to offer no-fee accounts while still generating revenue.

Your library’s app is usually Libby, since over 90% of North American public libraries use OverDrive, which makes it. Sign in with your library card to read on a phone, tablet, or Kobo e-reader, or to send most borrowed e-books to a Kindle if your library is in the U.S.

Industry observers note that the catch is the wait. Publishers often let a library lend each digital copy to just one reader at a time, so popular titles have wait lists. Place holds early, and if one becomes available while you’re reading another book, suspend it to keep your place in line.

For a title you’re watching, eReaderIQ, a free tracker, emails you when its Kindle price falls to the amount you set.

Say you borrow through Libby, read classics free, and pay about $2 for each deal you buy. Then Kindle+, formerly Kindle Unlimited, costs $11.99 a month plus tax, about what six $2 deals cost, but it only lends its books, up to 20 at a time, while deals are yours to keep. It pays for itself at seven or more of its books a month that you’d otherwise buy, so check that its catalog carries the authors you read.

For the next e-book you want, place a Libby hold and set an eReaderIQ alert at the price you’d pay, then take whichever comes first.

• Rewards that reinforce good financial behavior• A clean, easy to understand interface• A focus on progress instead of perfection• Motivation during the hardest part of the journey.

Yes. Debbie is a legitimate personal finance app built around a behavior-driven debt payoff model. While it won’t magically erase debt, it helps customers stay engaged, which is often the biggest missing piece in successfully paying off debt.

Paying off debt is rarely about knowledge. Most people already know what they should be doing. The real challenge is sticking with the plan month after month, even when progress feels slow.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you’re short on rent this month, call your landlord before it’s due and offer part of it now with a firm date for the rest, then get the deal in writing.
  • A week before rent is due, you’re offering your landlord a plan.
  • An eviction costs the landlord too, in court fees and in rent that goes unpaid while the case runs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re short on rent this month, call your landlord before it’s due and offer part of it now with a firm date for the rest, then get the deal in writing. The same day, call 211 or visit 211.org to reach local emergency rental assistance and charities that can cover the gap.

A week before rent is due, you’re offering your landlord a plan. A week after, you’re explaining a missed payment that may already carry a late fee.

An eviction costs the landlord too, in court fees and in rent that goes unpaid while the case runs. Offering part of the rent now and the rest by a set date gives your landlord a cheaper way to get paid than going to court.

Say your $1,000 rent is due on the first and you have $400. Call on the 25th and offer to pay the $400 on the first and the other $600 by the 20th. Ask whether your landlord will waive the late fee as long as you keep to the proposal, then send a text or email that restates the amounts and dates so you both have the deal in writing.

Then call 211 to find the $600. The federal rental assistance created during the pandemic ended in September 2025, so the money now comes from state and local programs, charities such as the Salvation Army and Catholic Charities, churches, and one-time emergency grants. A 211 specialist can tell you which of these serve your area. If you’re behind on other bills too, ask about emergency help with those bills on the same call.

Skip payday loans and cash advance apps. With both, you borrow against your next paycheck, which only moves the shortfall to next month’s rent. A common payday fee of $15 per $100 borrowed works out to an annual rate of almost 400% on a two-week loan, according to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.

It has been revealed that apply for help the same day you make the deal with your landlord. Rental assistance can take several weeks to arrive after you apply, and the rest of your rent is due on the date you promised.

#102938. Industry News: What Is Dollar Cost Averaging?

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Wellkeptwallet ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: What Is Dollar Cost Averaging?

📅 07 May 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1073 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Wellkeptwallet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If the idea of putting money into the stock market makes you nervous, you are not alone.
  • Dollar cost averaging is a strategy that takes that worry off the table.
  • In this article, we will explain how dollar cost averaging works, why so many long-term investors rely on it, and how to put it into practice starting today.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If the idea of putting money into the stock market makes you nervous, you are not alone. A lot of people hold back because they are afraid of buying at the wrong time.

Dollar cost averaging is a strategy that takes that worry off the table. Instead of trying to time the market perfectly, you invest a fixed amount on a regular schedule and let time do the heavy lifting.

In this article, we will explain how dollar cost averaging works, why so many long-term investors rely on it, and how to put it into practice starting today.

Dollar cost averaging (DCA) is an investment strategy in which you invest a fixed dollar amount in a specific asset at regular intervals, regardless of market conditions. Whether the market is up, down, or flat, you invest the same amount on the same schedule.

The result is that you end up buying more shares when prices are low and fewer shares when prices are high. Over time, this can lower your average cost per share compared to making a single lump-sum investment at the wrong moment.

Most people already practice dollar cost averaging without realizing it. If you contribute to a 401(k) every time you get a paycheck, that is dollar cost averaging in action.

The mechanics are straightforward. You pick an investment, decide on a fixed dollar amount, and choose a schedule. Every week, every two weeks, or every month, you invest that amount, no matter what the market is doing that day.

Because you are investing a fixed dollar amount rather than a fixed number of shares, your money automatically buys more shares when prices dip and fewer when prices climb. This built-in dynamic is what makes the strategy so useful for investors who want to build wealth steadily without spending hours watching the market.

Sources indicate that for most people, low-cost index funds are the best vehicle for this strategy. They give you broad diversification across hundreds of companies in a single investment, and their expense ratios are far lower than actively managed mutual funds or target-date funds. That difference in fees compounds significantly over decades.

According to recent reports, say you decide to invest $300 every month into a low-cost S&P 500 index fund. Here is what three months might look like:.

After three months, you have invested $900 and own 21 shares. Your average cost per share is $42.86. If you had invested all $900 in Month 1 at $50 per share, you would only own 18 shares. The dip in Month 2 actually worked in your favor because you had cash ready to put to work at a lower price.

This is the core idea. You stop worrying about whether today is a good day to invest and start focusing on building a consistent habit instead.

It removes emotion from investing.

One of the biggest mistakes investors make is letting fear and excitement drive their decisions. They pile in when the market is hot and pull out when it drops. Dollar-cost averaging sidesteps all of that by turning investing into a routine, like paying a bill, that runs automatically on a schedule.

It makes market downturns work for you.

Industry observers note that when markets fall, most people panic. With dollar cost averaging, a dip is simply an opportunity to buy more shares at a discount. If you stay consistent, you will naturally accumulate more of your investment when it is on sale.

It is accessible no matter your income.

You do not need a large lump sum to get started. Even small, consistent contributions can grow meaningfully over time thanks to compounding. A good starting point is to aim for at least 10% of your gross income going toward investments. If that feels like a stretch right now, start with whatever you can manage and increase it over time.

Consistency is the real edge in personal investing. Dollar cost averaging encourages exactly that. When you automate your contributions, investing happens in the background while you get on with your life.

Want a free tool to help you keep track of your investments? Check out Empower!

Dollar cost averaging is a sound strategy, but it is worth understanding its limits before you dive in.

According to recent reports, if you are investing in a low-quality asset that trends downward over time, buying it consistently will not save you. That is why what you invest in matters just as much as how you invest. Sticking to broad, low-cost index funds gives you exposure to the overall market rather than betting on a single firm’s performance. Investing heavily in individual stocks introduces a level of risk that most people do not need to take on.

Alternative investments should stay small.

According to recent reports, things like gold, cryptocurrency, and other alternative assets can have a place in a portfolio, but they should stay well under 10% of your total invested assets. These assets tend to be far more volatile and speculative than a diversified index fund, and there is no reason to let them dominate your long-term strategy.

A lump sum can outperform in a rising market.

Research has shown that if you have a large sum ready to invest, putting it all in at once tends to outperform dollar cost averaging over the long run, simply because markets go up more often than they go down. That stated, most people do not have a large lump sum sitting around. For those building wealth paycheck by paycheck, dollar cost averaging is the practical and sensible path.

Recent findings suggest that getting started with dollar cost averaging does not require a financial advisor or a complicated setup. Here is a simple framework:.

According to recent reports, dollar cost averaging is one of the most practical investing strategies available to everyday investors. It takes the guesswork out of market timing, helps you build a consistent habit, and naturally positions you to benefit from market dips over time.

The key is to pair this strategy with the right investments. Low-cost index funds are a strong foundation. They offer diversification, keep fees low, and have a long track record of rewarding patient investors. Avoid concentrating too much on single stocks or speculative alternatives, and keep contributing regularly regardless of what the market is doing on any given day.

If you stay the course and keep contributing, time becomes your greatest asset.

Sources indicate that having more than one type of debt is common, and that’s especially true once you graduate from college and start your first “real job.” You may have credit card debt, an auto loan, and a mortgage payment to make once you buy your first home. It’s also common to have other random debts to cover, including student loans.

If you’re like many who took out loans during college, you will likely be paying them off after you graduate. In fact, 82% of students who borrowed loans expect to be making payments post-graduation, according to a recent College Ave Student Loans survey.

That said, you’ll want to make sure you’re balancing debt repayment with your savings goals along the way.

According to recent reports, you’ll also want to make sure you’re paying down debts in the optimal order, or in a way that will help you save the most money on interest as possible while aligning with your goals. Which debts should you pay off first? Here’s a rundown of how to get the best results:.

No matter which types of debt you have, credit card debt should be your first priority. Why? Because credit card debt is likely the most expensive debt you have by far.

Federal Reserve data shows the average credit card interest rate on accounts assessed interest came in at around 22% as of May 2023, yet your credit card could easily be charging higher rates than the average.

Industry observers note that to save as much money as possible, you should strive to pay as much as you can toward high-interest credit card bills each month. You can also pay down credit card debt faster with the help of a debt consolidation loan or a 0% APR balance transfer credit card.

Sources indicate that other unsecured debts like personal loan debt should come next in the debt payoff pecking order. After all, unsecured debts tend to have higher interest rates than secured debts like auto loans. In fact, the Federal Reserve also reported that the average interest rate on a 24-month personal loan came in at 11.48% as of May 2023, compared to the average rate of 7.81% on a 60-month auto loan.

Ideally, you’ll start paying more toward personal loan debt and other unsecured debts after all credit card debt is entirely paid off, although you should make at least the minimum payment on all your bills throughout the entire process.

Sources indicate that the next debt you’ll want to tackle is your student loans. I suggest focusing on these loans after other unsecured debts, since federal student loans (and many private student loans) come with low fixed interest rates and monthly payments that will not change over time. If you have federal student loans, you may even want to look into income-driven repayment looks.

If you’re hoping to pay down student loans faster or just want to save money on interest, you can also consider refinancing your student loans to get a shorter repayment timeline, a lower monthly payment, or both. Just remember that refinancing federal student loans can mean losing access to income-driven repayment looks and federal protections like deferment and forbearance.

Sources indicate that once you have paid off or substantially paid down all your other debts, you can focus your efforts on secured debts you have like mortgage loans and auto loans. These debts should be dealt with last since they are secured with collateral and tend to offer lower interest rates as a result. For example, you can consider paying more than the minimum on your mortgage, a car loan, or both until they’re paid off completely.

It has been revealed that then again, you may want to pay off debts with extremely low interest rates as slowly as possible to free up more cash flow for living expenses and investments. If you took out a mortgage in January of 2021 when the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed rate home loan was as low as 2.65%, for example, it makes sense to make the minimum payment on that debt and invest your extra cash instead.

According to recent reports, it’s notable to make sure you balance debt repayment with other financial considerations. After all, focusing too much on debt repayment early in life can leave you behind when it comes to investing for retirement or saving up for a first home.

While you’ll want to eliminate credit card debt and other high-interest debts as swiftly as you can, even if you have to stop saving and investing for a while, you can pay down student loan debt and secured debts at a slower pace while saving and investing for the future along the way.

Sources indicate that finally, make sure you have adequate emergency savings throughout your entire debt payoff journey, or that you begin saving for emergencies as soon as you can. Without a fully funded emergency fund, you can end up relying on credit cards and other loans to get by and ruin your debt payoff progress in the process.

How much should you save? While most experts recommend having an emergency fund that can cover three to six months of expenses, it’s okay to start small if you have to.

Having more than one type of debt is how it works for most people, especially when you’re young and in the early stages of your career. When it comes to paying it off, however, you’ll want to make sure you have a concrete plan that can help you reduce interest charges and get where you want to be.

Industry observers note that focusing on credit card debt and other unsecured debts first always makes sense, since these debts aren’t secured by an asset and tend to charge much higher interest rates. You can focus on student loans next, followed by other secured debts you have like a home loan or car loan.

In the meantime, make sure you have an adequate emergency fund and invest in it for retirement. After all, debt won’t last forever if you’re serious about repayment, and saving and investing early can help you benefit from compound interest and avoid using credit cards for surprise expenses. Creating a budget to track these factors is your best bet.

If you need help creating one, or simply don’t know where to start, use this budget worksheet as your guide – you’ll reach financial freedom in no time.
